## Purpose

The reflog (reference log) serves as a local-only, time-limited safety net that records every position HEAD and branch references have pointed to. This includes commits that are no longer reachable from any branch following a reset or rebase operation.

## Recovery from destructive operations

When a reset or rebase goes wrong—such as accidentally losing work or resetting to the wrong commit—the reflog allows developers to recover those "lost" commits. Because the reflog records intermediate states that remain in the local repository even after they become unreachable via normal branch navigation, you can use it to find and check out the commit you actually want.

This is the primary safety mechanism for recovering from local accidents:

- Reflog entries persist for commits that would otherwise be unreachable (garbage-collected)
- You can inspect the reflog to find the exact commit position before the destructive operation
- Recovery is as simple as checking out or resetting back to the appropriate reflog entry

## Local scope

The reflog is fundamentally local to a single repository clone:

- Reflog entries are **never pushed** to a remote repository
- They do **not** exist on a fresh clone — each repository has its own reflog history
- This means recovery from the reflog is an option only for the repository where the accident occurred
